import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Data provided as a string
data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Set a clean aesthetic style for the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axes for the plot

# Create a scatter plot to visualize relationships between several features

    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',
    size='weight_grams',
    sizes=(80, 800),  # Adjust the range of marker sizes for better visual distinction

    markers={0: 'X', 1: 'o'},  # Use 'X' for no 4K video (0), 'o' for 4K video (1)

# Adjust plot layout to make sure everything fits, especially the legend
plt.tight_layout()
